title: The Winter Uniform
premise: In the winter of 1911, Ada Halloran is sent to repair the master clock of a remote mountain observatory, only to find its astronomer dead and his final observations — proof of a falsified star catalogue that will ruin a powerful academy — hidden inside the clock's case. When the season's first storm closes the bridge and the observatory's patrons arrive to destroy the evidence, Ada must choose between her instinct for invisibility and her duty to a dead man's truth. Smuggling the plates past three checkpoints before the river ice breaks, she loses her apprenticeship, nearly loses her life, and finally understands that history is made by whoever refuses to look away. The book ends with Ada testifying in the city as the ice breaks behind her, the truth published under both her name and the astronomer's.
about_author: Xanthe Sandoval is the pen name of a former horology restorer who spent a decade repairing tower clocks in alpine towns before turning to fiction. Her work is known for meticulous period detail and quiet heroines who discover their own courage late, and reluctantly.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In her master's workshop, Ada repairs a merchant's watch while reflecting that great events happen to other people, elsewhere. She is summoned to the mountain observatory to fix its famous master clock. Emotional beat: contentment built on deliberate smallness.

chapters.title: Up Where the Air Thins
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The ascent by carriage and foot; first sight of the observatory dome against a bruising sky. She meets the staff: housekeeper Frau Brenner, assistant Kessler, and the aloof director Voss. Emotional beat: awe shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: A Clock That Keeps Wrong Time
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The master clock runs but hesitates at odd intervals, as if obstructed. Opening the case, she finds tools not her own and scratches counting down from thirty. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Astronomer's Last Night
chapters.summary: Kessler's POV, tense and evasive. He recounts Dr. Lindqvist's final weeks: obsessions with certain star plates, arguments with Voss, a fall on the ice stairs ruled accidental. Emotional beat: guilt wearing the mask of loyalty.

chapters.title: What the Case Conceals
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Behind the escapement she finds a oilcloth packet: photographic plates proving the academy's celebrated catalogue was fabricated from one night's data. Emotional beat: the vertigo of holding something that changes everything.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The storm arrives early; the bridge is chained for the season. Voss announces the academy inspectors will come when it reopens — and asks pointed questions about Lindqvist's papers. Emotional beat: trapped, and newly responsible.

chapters.title: Frau Brenner's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Frau Brenner's POV. Over bread and stew, the housekeeper reveals she loved Lindqvist like a son and suspects the fall was no accident. She warns Ada that Voss searches rooms. Emotional beat: unexpected alliance, maternal ferocity.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Gate
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Voss institutes bag inspections at the observatory gate after a plate goes missing from the archive. Ada hides the packet inside a broken pendulum bob awaiting repair. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into craft.

chapters.title: The Man Who Watches the Ice
chapters.summary: New character Marta's POV — the ferryman's daughter stranded on the near bank. She tells Ada about the river's spring break-up and an old smugglers' path along the gorge. Emotional beat: hope with a price attached.

chapters.title: Voss Offers a Bargain
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Voss privately offers Ada a permanent post and her master's debt forgiven if she surrenders 'any stray effects' of Lindqvist's. She lies to his face for the first time. Emotional beat: temptation met and refused.

chapters.title: Kessler Breaks
chapters.summary: Kessler's POV. Haunted, he confesses he helped Voss alter the catalogue and let Lindqvist's death go unquestioned. He gives Ada the archive key but cannot bring himself to testify. Emotional beat: cowardice and conscience in the same body.

chapters.title: The Search
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. While Ada is summoned away, Voss tears apart her room and finds the empty pendulum bob. Frau Brenner covers by claiming the bob for scrap. But now Voss knows someone has the plates. Emotional beat: hunted.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Stair
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Descending the gorge path at night with the plates sewn into her coat, Ada is stopped by the observatory's watchman at the mid-station hut. Marta's distraction lets her pass. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Frostbite and False Leads
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. The two women shelter in the ferryman's hut; Marta reveals she owes Voss money and has been reporting movements. She chooses, at last, to lie to him instead. Emotional beat: betrayal confessed, loyalty remade.

chapters.title: What History Owes the Dead
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Waiting out a whiteout, Ada reads Lindqvist's letters to his sister and understands why he hid the truth rather than flee: he wanted it found by someone who would finish the work. Emotional beat: inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The valley tollhouse, where Voss himself waits, having guessed her route. A cat-and-mouse conversation over tea; he nearly takes the packet. Kessler arrives unexpectedly and swears the plates were destroyed. Emotional beat: salvation from the least likely hand.

chapters.title: The Ice Begins to Groan
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The river cracks; the bridge may open within days. Voss telegraphs the academy that a thief holds stolen property. Ada realizes testimony alone won't survive — the plates must reach a newspaper before the inspectors do. Emotional beat: the clock running down.

chapters.title: Across the Breaking River
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax part one. With the bridge still chained, Marta poles her across the rotting ice at dawn. The plates are lost to the water — or seem to be. Ada carries instead Lindqvist's letters and her own sworn account. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and the discovery that memory is also evidence.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Clock Room
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax part two. Returning through the tunnel to confront Voss, she finds him burning the archive. Kessler stops his hand; Frau Brenner locks the door. Ada forces Voss to hear the ticking of the master clock — Lindqvist's message, still keeping honest time. Emotional beat: the invisible woman made unignorable.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the city, before the academy tribunal and a newspaper editor, Ada gives her account; Kessler corroborates despite his terror; the recovered plates — fished from the shallows by Marta's father — are produced. Emotional beat: trembling voice, steady hands.

chapters.title: The Catalogue Corrected
chapters.summary: Frau Brenner's POV. Weeks later: the corrected catalogue published under Lindqvist's name and Ada Halloran's; Voss resigns in disgrace. At the observatory, a new apprentice arrives to learn the master clock. Emotional beat: grief settling into legacy.

chapters.title: What Ada Keeps
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Back in the workshop, Ada repairs the merchant's watch again — the same small work, but no longer a hiding place. She hangs Lindqvist's scratched count above her bench, finished at zero. Emotional beat: identity claimed; history understood as something you do, not something that happens.
